newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU declines comment on Unilever ice cream sales.
newsitem.headline: EU declines comment on Unilever ice cream sales.

text.p: The European Commission declined to comment on Monday on a news report that it was about to reopen a probe into Unilever's selling arrangements for ice cream in Ireland.
Shares in Unilever Plc dropped early in the day after a report in the Financial Times said the Mars company had resumed its attack on Unilever's ice cream sales practices.

The FT said Mars had attacked Unilever's sales practices in the Irish republic involving the supply of freezers to shopkeepers for stocking its brands. However, Unilever spokesman Mike Haines dismissed the Mars claims, saying "Our business is not designed to reduce consumer choice, and it does not do so. It is fair competition."
Commission spokesman Willy Helin said, "The Commission does not comment on the presentation of their case by parties to Commission proceedings."

Helin was asked to react to the article which said the Commission would send Unilever a "statement of objections" later this week outlining fresh grievances against the Anglo-Dutch consumer foods giant.
The Commission in 1995 dropped proceedings against Unilever subsidiary Van den Bergh Foods Ltd after Unilever agreed to change its ice cream distribution arrangements.

This included commitments to introduce a freezer cabinet hire-purchase scheme that would enable Irish retailers to buy their own cabinet; to charge a different price for retailers not taking Unilever freezers; and, more importantly, to sell off 1,750 cabinets as a means of freeing up shops.
Mars claims the commitments have not been respected.
